nodes.name: agent-api
nodes.description: unit control-plane; dispatch -> runtime spawn; meeting copilot Per-user ChatGPT disconnect keeps TINA/ASR sessions separate. Terminal OAuth state is cancelled locally; authenticated internal Agent API owns profile writes, disconnect and generation checks under the same file lock as token refresh. Credentials stay in the private auth volume; callbacks from a disconnected generation cannot restore an old account. Existing in-flight workers may retain short-lived tokens. Owner-scoped meeting Q&A reads canonical transcript and explicitly selected linked private Wiki documents, validates source IDs, stores source fingerprints, and creates a new Wiki page only after explicit Apply; existing pages and canonical data are never overwritten. Routine files are owner-scoped active private-workspace resources: anchored no-symlink I/O, per-owner serialized reconcile, source SHA preconditions for explicit Edit/toggle/delete, and stable IDs per workspace/file. Delete removes the source before cancelling all related jobs; shared workspace files never grant schedules. Chat dispatch serializes configuration changes per thread in Redis using expiring locks and keyed model-configuration digests under agent:chat-config:*. Raw credentials are never stored in that metadata. An unchanged configuration reuses its warm worker; changed provider, credential or model waits for the previous turn-complete and requests cooperative stop through the existing chat input stream, confirms terminal state through runtime.v1 and replaces the idle workload before pre-delivering and spawning the next turn. Busy or unverifiable refreshes return actionable errors without sending the prompt to an old provider. The existing thread id, output stream and provider-session history are preserved. Bedrock model discovery reads paginated regional foundation-model/inference-profile lists; credential tests use native InvokeModel. The API image packages the same Python provider helpers and automatic thinking policy as the worker. All providers use automatic thinking; legacy effort pins are ignored, and the settings UI exposes no manual thinking field. Worker configuration digests include the deployed provider-adapter revision, so adapter fixes replace old warm workers without discarding conversation history. Gemini defaults to gemini-3.5-flash. Gemini, DeepSeek and Bedrock credential tests verify native function-call/result round trips before reporting success; Bedrock uses the same InvokeModelWithResponseStream protocol as its CLI and decodes complete AWS event-stream frames with checksum validation; custom API model registration supplies exact model IDs to the pinned CLI SDK rather than embedding endpoint URIs. Groq credential tests verify a real function-call/result round trip through the worker request adapter before testing summaries. Model discovery excludes speech-only Orpheus entries and marks known text-only ALLaM as summary-only, preventing chat selection while preserving meeting use. Explicit /research chat commands and document research requests resolve a private writable note destination from the authenticated active set. Private Codex history restores turn-scoped recorded source metadata and original opened URLs; missing reference mappings remain visibly unresolved. Voice API traces use the bot request UUID forwarded in an internal header and carry it as separate worker dispatch metadata. Structured logs include only stages/status, duration and source counts; no source text, questions or credentials. Whole-meeting recaps use the existing three-worker background pool and one 120-second map/select/verify waiting budget. Computation is request-UUID scoped and never returns a partial summary as whole-meeting evidence. Each stage probes the internal owner/service-authenticated Meeting API turn permit before and after inference, in addition to source/policy checks; stopped/replaced turns cannot authorize further stages or late publication.

nodes.name: bot
nodes.description: Spawned-per-meeting worker: join -> capture -> selected ASR -> transcript.v1. Opt-in Google Meet voice reuses original ASR hypotheses before LocalAgreement, accepts local LiveKit WakeWord acoustic calls for TINA ơi/hey TINA, assembles same-channel bounded source-clock questions, fences duplicate/late windows and preserves transcript. Separate native VAD and KWS children; verified answer sentences use shared local TTS plus existing Stop. Owner diagnostics use allowlisted reason codes and at most three ASR prefix words; no full question/provider errors enter logs. Voice-only VAD endpoints advance the same ASR window below minimum/cadence, reuse covered results and serialize uncovered tails without closing/resetting transcript state. Content-free request-correlated timing logs separate acknowledgment from answer playback and preserve source clocks. Voice onset is distinct from retained pre-roll, and buffer generation/deferred-close fences run before hypothesis observation. Receive audio uses a separate meeting_rx sink; tts_sink feeds an always-available virtual_mic source. TTS sink mute plus verified Meet UI gate speech; system source mute is never used as a speech gate. Playback requires observed meeting microphone state after a bounded single-toggle verification and bounded device-recovery wait; blocked or unknown state fails closed. Bounded content-free audio counters observe the unchanged capture tee and same ASR requests; per-frame telemetry never adds HTTP calls. Opt-in NS runs after original archive taps and before both ASR and Silero. Off is synchronous bypass; timeout/overload/error drains only unacknowledged raw packets once, fences late outputs, and exposes failed mode. Capture stops before NS drain and ASR finalization.

nodes.name: transcription
nodes.description: transcription — OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions boundary with selectable backends: faster-whisper/CTranslate2, Apple MLX/Metal, and loopback FunASR Qwen3-ASR with FSMN-VAD. Clients send bounded audio windows, continuity prompts and content-free capture-lag metadata. FunASR exposes asr-status.v1 with actual device, bounded request timing samples, queue and model percentiles; Terminal reads it through a verified admin proxy. Browser render timings remain local. Does not write any redis carrier (the bot XADDs segments). Optional native Rust backend runs Silero VAD and Qwen3-ASR-0.6B INT8 through sherpa-onnx on CPU at host loopback :18001; it preserves VAD segment offsets and the same ASR status contract. The FunASR adapter forwards min_silence_duration_ms to FSMN max_end_silence_time (100-2000 ms, default 800 ms, explicitly pinned), preserving per-VAD sentence offsets for downstream alignment. An isolated single-source Apple Silicon PoC under deploy/transcription/streaming-poc validates real Qwen Transformers decoder token callbacks and paced growing-window hypotheses on cached VI/EN evaluation clips. It is not a selected production endpoint, does not claim an incremental audio encoder, and never changes/restarts production services; private external artifacts record token timing, accuracy, RAM and before/after listener identities. Sub-200 ms FunASR inputs receive trailing silence only in the temporary inference file to avoid incomplete FSMN frames; source PCM, reported duration and sentence bounds retain the original source interval. Empty input and inference failures remain errors. Optional authenticated loopback :18002 backend composes FunASR FSMN-VAD CPU with hash-pinned Gipformer 1.5 INT8 via Sherpa-ONNX OfflineRecognizer. The root Compose asr profile runs that same CPU service, mounts the pinned model directory and owns host port 18002 while enabled; unload the host LaunchAgent to avoid a port conflict. Existing Custom endpoint settings select it for Desktop/Bot without altering the Qwen platform default. Original VAD sample offsets survive speech slicing; no word timing, prompt conditioning, language detection or token streaming is claimed. One inference plus three bounded waiters, no audio/text in diagnostics. Optional native VieGem-ASR + KenLM endpoint at loopback :18005 uses separately pinned VieGem and EmbeddingGemma 2 assets, PyTorch FP32 on explicit MPS/CPU/CUDA, FSMN on CPU and upstream 4-gram CTC prefix beam decoding. It shares the authenticated bounded HTTP worker with Gipformer; inference is serialized and source VAD offsets stay on the original timeline. Installation does not select the endpoint globally. No incremental streaming, word alignment or automatic transcript polish is claimed; VieGem use is restricted by its non-commercial research license and Gemma terms. Identity also exposes the named viegem backend: administrators configure viegem_url in the platform transcription registry and a dotenvx-encrypted TINA_VIEGEM_TOKEN is injected at deployment startup (legacy database token supported only without that env); native startup decrypts its separate private env file strictly, user preferences select the backend name, and internal Bot/Desktop/dictation resolution carries only its registry-owned endpoint credential. Custom endpoints do not inherit the VieGem platform token; the browser-facing admin settings edge treats that credential as write-only. The source-build entrypoint resolves TINA_VIEGEM_DEVICE=auto to native MPS on Apple Silicon or Docker CUDA on Linux/Windows WSL2. Only the CTC model/encoder uses the GPU; FSMN and KenLM remain CPU. Actual MPS/CUDA compute and authenticated audio must pass before deployment succeeds; no silent CPU fallback. CUDA adds an owned Compose overlay with pinned cu130 wheels and one GPU reservation for inference only. MPS excludes the Docker VieGem profile and stops only the old owned CPU service before binding the same host endpoint; native startup failure attempts to restore that prior service while reporting failure. Explicit cpu remains available. Gipformer and token-free Docker model-install jobs are independent; native setup prepares the same pinned cache before activation. Inference mounts cached weights read-only, runtime tokens come from dotenvx and private keys are not mounted. make-down also removes/stops the owned MPS LaunchAgent. Only a fresh registry receives a VieGem default; existing preferences and foreign worker ownership are preserved. Per-account ASR runtime control keeps shared workers alive while any enabled account requests them. A derived-key authenticated drain fence refuses new requests and cannot stop a worker with active inference. CUDA hardware validation remains pending on a real NVIDIA host. VieGem has an optional operator-only bounded name prior, default zero/off; paired local name experiments do not alter production tuning without evidence.

nodes.name: desktop
nodes.description: all-in-one dev host: bot+collector+gateway in one process; capture sessions resolve central identity ASR settings once (personal API key > platform > environment), pin the selection until stop and expose credential-free backend metadata Local SQLite journal preserves confirmed ASR, PCM source timestamps and owner corrections across restarts; document/review/audio routes consult canAccess. Explicit post-meeting second-pass ASR yields persisted proposals; one worker pauses between utterances for live capture and never edits text before owner Apply.; input ring shared with ASR, per-session/source sample clock and original capture timestamp archived in SQLite; authorized audio-timeline.v1 metadata and RAM-to-archive range reads never fill missing samples; WS /ws fans out transcript.v1 confirmed/pending frames to local capture clients; vi-en pending ASR language reviews archive original/retry text plus source PCM separately from confirmed transcript; owner/origin-checked asr-reviews routes and review UI expose suggestions without adding them to canonical or memory. Ingest ready advertises recording_ack and recording_resume for an optional client_session nonce. REC1 acknowledgements follow sink processing; explicit finalization closes immediately while unexpected socket closes retain the recording assembler for 30 seconds for same-client resume. Shutdown flushes pending assemblers. Different logical client sessions finalize separately; replacing a current recording master preserves the older file as a versioned sibling. Opt-in audio_ack=sample-range.v1 requires indexed PCM and a client_session nonce; exact-range audio-ack follows durable journal insertion. Persistent archive session ids deduplicate identical PCM/timestamps across reconnect and process restart without duplicate pipeline feed; conflicting/overlapping ranges fail without ACK. Socket-local pipeline RAM stays separate from archive identity. Audio ACK does not promise downstream ASR completion. A single background ASR recovery worker resumes unprocessed source/sample ranges after stop or restart, using bounded 15-second archive windows and the existing Gmeet ASR/filter engine. It yields to live capture, retries failures with backoff, pins an opaque backend/credential digest, and never substitutes an unavailable configuration. Owner/origin-scoped asr-recovery.v1 exposes jobs and checkpoints. Recovered mixed audio stays unattributed; known channel names and local mic identity are preserved. Live confirmed segments project accepted canonical text at the gateway; drafts for edited/restored ids are suppressed. transcript.v1 binary/event shapes are unchanged and revision metadata remains on the separate transcript.revised/HTTP interfaces. Owner-only stt-foundation.v1 snapshots persist a journal instance and monotonic sequence; globally stable meeting/source/segment IDs retain exact sample references and accepted revision history. stt-metrics.v1 distinguishes bounded ASR-call, capture lag, SQLite persistence, caption and client-reported foreground UI timing; no text/audio in metrics. Mixed lane transcript IDs include connection and source channel so mic/tab/reconnect turn counters cannot collide. STT diagnostics separate confirmed-caption publication delay from draft-window age; the legacy combined series remains available. Capture teardown plans missing source/sample ranges instead of blanket-checkpointing received PCM; only confirmed or successfully committed recovery ranges advance ASR coverage. Historical checkpoints are preserved. Late accepted PCM atomically reopens completed ASR sessions before ACK so appended tails remain recoverable. Batch archive recovery selects the existing mixed media/repetition filter through the Gmeet host policy hook, retaining short single-word speech while RMS/confidence/language checks remain in force; live Gmeet defaults and completed historical jobs are unchanged. Desktop owns a meeting-local SQLite speaker registry: channel 1000 is one local microphone identity, raw 1002 is archive-only, verified Meet participant IDs bind distinct people, and system mix 999 stays unknown. Owner rename/assignment uses independent speaker revisions and the durable metadata outbox. Owner-triggered post-meeting diarization sends verified saved system audio to the existing authenticated loopback worker; proposals require explicit Apply with registry, text, timeline and audio-hash checks. Manual names/unknown and participant identities are protected. Owner-only canonical and meeting-memory endpoints share accepted speaker projection; drafts/raw mic never become evidence, and words remain segment_fallback without forced alignment. HTTP Window ASR defaults remain unchanged. Owner-triggered post-meeting MFA alignment batches up to 20 verified continuous mono PCM16 clips, at most 30 seconds each, over current accepted text. Alignment jobs yield between batches to live capture and serialize with refinement/diarization. Per-segment accepted timing publishes only after expected text revision, text/audio hashes and capture source references still match. Word audio playback rechecks provenance and never assigns time to OOV tokens. Text edits and Restore invalidate timing atomically. Canonical words/phrases use source-absolute times; speaker attribution is reprojected from the current registry and applied acoustic turns. Alignment types, hashing, validation and speaker projection live in the pure alignment-model module; transcript-journal depends on that model, while the alignment worker depends on the journal, without a runtime import cycle.

nodes.name: agent-worker
nodes.description: spawned isolated workspace-agent worker; selectable Claude Code, Codex app-server, or Antigravity CLI (agy) harness; every dispatch mounts the ordered [_global, active workspaces, _system] stack, fails closed without _global, and loads its authoritative entry context. Groq mode reuses Codex against the fixed Groq Responses endpoint for chat and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions for meeting summaries. A per-turn Groq model profile disables unsupported freeform patch tools and namespace delegation at the CLI source, with provider-neutral TINA instructions and file edits through the existing sandboxed function tools. DeepSeek mode reuses Claude Code against DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint for chat and its Chat Completions endpoint for summaries. Gemini mode selects agy's Gemini API-key provider for chat and the Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint for summaries, without consumer/OAuth credentials or a synthetic Terms acknowledgment. Dispatch selects each effective per-user/platform key for both paths and clears other providers' credentials. A temporary authenticated loopback proxy inside the worker strips unsupported Responses fields and non-function tools, maps developer instructions to system messages for non-GPT-OSS chat templates without changing tool history, rejects known non-tool chat models, serializes function calls and preserves streamed events and HTTP errors; it never executes tools or expands the harness grants. Codex pins explicit named per-turn filesystem profiles to TINA write grants, protects agent/Git metadata and excludes temporary write roots. Trusted chat/routine turns map WebSearch/WebFetch grants to cached/live hosted web tools; untrusted event/transcription turns disable web tools and remain read-only/offline. Shell networking requires Bash plus WebFetch and a root-owned exclusive GitHub-domain proxy policy, with private addresses, upstream proxies, Unix-socket forwarding and direct-network bypass blocked. Managed networking is not globally forced so offline turns remain isolated. Codex loads workspace instructions and skills, maps TINA auto/gate MCP grants to Codex approval modes, streams tool lifecycle events, pauses gate calls for owner-scoped, one-call decisions over chat streams using tool-approval.v1, and participates in the shared transcript-size resume cap. A private per-TINA-session provider-thread index preserves display history across provider restarts; reset removes this index, and legacy recovery uses only same-subject, same-session Redis events newer than session creation. Codex user-message events define visible human messages, excluding injected environment and developer context; restored tool names remain descriptive. Antigravity maps TINA mount grants to read_file/write_file permissions, sandboxes commands, loads governed skills, exposes only auto-granted non-secret MCP servers in headless mode, and normalizes streamed events and conversation ids. The legacy Antigravity model selection requires a persisted Terms warning acknowledgment; consumer OAuth access through third-party software is prohibited by Google's terms. The Gemini API-key provider has independent credential preflight. Harness-written kg/entities files are workspace.v1-validated before commit. Post-meeting summary uses a tool-less CompletionPort and a deterministic writer with a local generated-content fingerprint, inference-time compare-and-swap, workspace locking and atomic publication; user-edited or unmarked existing documents are preserved, and only the meeting entity path is committed. Meeting Q&A uses a private short-lived, tool-less CompletionPort job with read-only mounts and no public chat history. Web-enabled Codex turns render explicit source metadata as final Markdown links and persist bounded per-turn source records in private continuity; missing citation mappings are never guessed. Explicit Knowledge research instructions create a new private Markdown note with meeting/repo/web source rows, evidence versions and verification dates, preserving other files and canonical transcript/audio. Voice jobs optionally request provider-side JSON Schema for answers/plans/review, restricted to authorized source IDs; explicit unsupported-format responses alone use the validated legacy path. Retrieval sets above eight excerpts get one optional four-second HTTP-timeout selected-model rerank, selecting up to 12 IDs plus recent/heard-history references within 32 excerpts/24000 characters. Invalid/empty rankings and oversized pinned context retain the original retrieval; verification and repair always receive the full original evidence. Ranking consumes the existing voice scheduling deadline. Content-free UUID-correlated stage logs cover selection, model calls, review and repair.

nodes.name: TINA Capture
nodes.description: Tauri/Rust macOS 15+ client: explicit meeting capture of microphone and system audio plus hold-to-dictate from a global Fn shortcut. Separate source channels are validated, resampled to 16 kHz with SpeexDSP and sent as capture.v1 to local Desktop. Native Capture does not link Sherpa/ONNX for resampling, avoiding incompatible KissFFT symbols between Sherpa and fixed-point Speex. Resampler float samples use PCM16 units internally and return normalized PCM; packet boundaries do not change the output waveform. Default dual-source capture uses Speex AEC plus residual echo suppression with channel 999 as far-end reference, preserves raw mic on archive-only channel 1002 and routes processed mic on channel 1000 to ASR. Aligned dual-source blocks additionally use a stateful 70 Hz high-pass on mic/reference and Speex denoising capped at -3 dB; AGC/VAD remain off and no samples are gated out. TINA_MIC_CLEANUP=0 restores AEC plus residual-only behavior; TINA_SPEEX_RESIDUAL_SUPPRESSION=0 keeps linear AEC only and TINA_SPEEX_AEC=0 uses raw mic. Capture Diagnostics distinguishes configured AEC from actual processed blocks, reports bypassed samples and source mic clipping, and exposes setup fallback reasons without audio or text. Pause/resume clears pending audio and DSP state while retaining session counters. Missing sample-index.v1, DSP initialization failure or unavailable reference passes original mic through. CoreAudio process metadata raises a non-focusable detect/record/ended overlay for allowlisted meeting apps after a 5 s sustain; capture never auto-starts, pause drops frames and freezes the elapsed clock, and a meeting-end reminder offers a 15 s keep-recording grace. Live captions subscribe to Desktop WS /ws, keep a rolling confirmed/pending window for the floating subtitle window, and never affect audio. Markdown export reads the Desktop transcript. Dictation uses microphone only; after stop, Desktop may forward only final transcript text through the authenticated polish bridge, while TINA Capture keeps raw ASR available for copy/restore and pastes raw text if polish is unavailable. No screen images or active-app contents are read; no model or service credentials are loaded in this process.

nodes.name: Desktop transcript journal
nodes.description: Local SQLite WAL: durable meetings, immutable per-source Float32 PCM timeline and original ASR with compare-and-swap correction history. Single writer Desktop. Audio cap 2 GiB/session is surfaced as archive incomplete; ASR continues. Stores refinement jobs/proposals and atomic apply with ASR model/audio hash provenance. Canonical FTS5 current-text index and transactional revision outbox, rebuilt/replayed across restart. Additive asr_language_reviews table stores pending original/retry results and Float32 request audio, deduplicated per meeting/session/PCM hash; 90-second request and 256 MiB per-meeting audio limits. Additive audio_capture_sessions maps meeting/client nonce to persistent archive id; audio_chunks acts as durable exact sample-range receipt with byte/timestamp comparison and overlap rejection. Existing 2 GiB session quota includes pre-restart bytes. Additive asr_sessions, asr_windows and asr_coverage persist routing digests, source/sample jobs and processed intervals; speaker_name is stored with audio chunks. Live confirmed text and its coverage commit atomically. Recovery transcript, FTS index, sample checkpoint and completed job share one SQLite transaction. Running jobs become retryable after process restart. Historical PCM without routing metadata is not auto-decoded. Additive journal_metadata and foundation_versions retain source authority identity and export sequence across restart. Additive speaker_registries, diarization_jobs and canonical_projections persist independent speaker revisions, source-bound proposals and canonical projection versions. Speaker updates and speaker-revision.v1 outbox commit atomically; raw PCM/text remain unchanged. Speaker-aware stt-foundation.v1 exports preserve optional speaker ID/revision. Additive alignment_jobs and alignment_results store accepted-text timing independent from raw ASR; transcript_sequences supplies monotonic metadata invalidation sequences independent of text history length. Alignment result and metadata-only event commit in one SQLite transaction. Original source timestamps and accepted/raw text never change during alignment.

nodes.name: transcript-refinement.v1
nodes.description: Owner-only second-pass ASR proposals for Desktop and clocked bot recordings. Optional fixed vocabulary; explicit revision-safe Apply and immutable raw Restore. Bot refinement optionally pins bounded gain for quiet clips, retaining original sample timing/hash and recording prepared-input provenance and last ASR HTTP duration. A bounded local A/B evaluation tool measures accent-preserving CER/token/boundary metrics without modifying application data. Saved bot clips preserve packet timestamps through a bounded coarse seek and trim on the 16 kHz sample clock; absent audio beyond 1 ms is rejected without padding. Apply retains prepared-input provenance in immutable correction history even after later jobs or Restore. Bot review compares Unicode-preserving repetition/non-lexical text cues with original-clip quiet-frame evidence, and checks second-pass suggestions against those same acoustics. Source and proposal checks remain advisory, revision-bound and owner-only; no speech-absence claim, automatic deletion or Apply.

An answer may include up to four additional individually authorized meetings with namespaced sources and source-meeting audio. Retrieval ranks within each meeting and allocates excerpt/character budgets in rounds across meetings with evidence. Related documents resolve aliased, encoded and relative wikilinks after reviewed moves. When a saved Wiki page moves, frontmatter identity locates it in the same visible workspace; locked Apply reuses that page, preserves edited content and refuses ambiguous copies instead of recreating the old path. Missing or revoked meetings redact stored claims and quotes. Source fingerprints are rechecked after inference, on answer review, Apply and Wiki opening; this is cross-store freshness checking, not a distributed transaction. Source-bound fact reviews live in reviews/{fact_id}.json with explicit approved/discarded/pending state, edited display text and review CAS; canonical facts and raw audio/text are unchanged.

nodes.name: Explicit private Markdown document edits
nodes.description: Owner-authorized content document PUT, no-overwrite move and explicit delete with expected SHA-256, existing workspace write lock, entity frontmatter validation and atomic file replacement. Reviewed moves preview source-preserving static backlinks and outgoing relative links in the same workspace; confirmation rechecks the full plan fingerprint, preserves code and aliases, reports ambiguous/uneditable references, rolls back ordinary write failures and removes the source last. Bounded Unicode Markdown content search excludes hidden paths and symlinks. Dashboard uses source-preserving formatting, a folder tree, wikilinks, history and per-account/workspace/file draft recovery across reloads via browser session storage retaining the original SHA-256; Terminal searches its authorized active mounts. Explicit per-path Git commit leaves unrelated staged paths and remotes untouched; shared workspaces remain read-only here. General harness writers retain their existing filesystem behavior.

nodes.name: Optional Vietnamese TTS sidecar
nodes.description: Optional separate Compose service under deploy/tts: one preset VieNeu v3 Turbo ONNX CPU voice. Authenticated OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech consumes bounded text and returns headerless mono PCM16 at 24 kHz. Pinned model/codec snapshots are operator-downloaded, hash-verified and read-only; runtime hub access is offline. One synthesis at a time; no transcript writes, agent imports or speech text logging. Native synthesis is not preemptible; existing bot Stop cancels its HTTP request/playback. Shared env stores a Dotenvx-encrypted token; a host runner loads only that token with a separate private key. Model cache paths are per-host; TTS keys are not injected into inference. Also available in main Compose speech profile. FIFO synthesis queue has at most three waiters, 15s queue timeout and drops disconnected queued clients. Exactly one fixed source-free acknowledgment is prewarmed/cached; private meeting answers are never cached. TTS derives a bounded spoken copy from unchanged display input using the pinned normalizer for selected numeric spans and an operator-owned image-packaged pronunciation dictionary. Explicit invocation meeting IDs map to projects; default-only preview and unknown meetings do not inherit another project. Clients cannot supply dictionaries. Custom preprocessing excludes code/URLs/email; no speech text is logged or saved over canonical text. Bot serializes validated answer sentences and checks policy before each sentence. Native infer_stream yields chunked PCM24 with stateful soxr resampling and one final flush. HTTP failure after headers omits the chunk terminator; cancellation closes the generator between native calls while retaining bounded FIFO admission and absolute deadlines. Bot buffers 150ms and keeps at most current plus one lookahead stream, bounded by PassThrough backpressure. Lookahead never opens mic; its failure cannot mute current audio. Stop, source-policy changes and departure cancel both handles; completed requires normal HTTP end and player/mic cleanup. Three-meeting operation keeps one native synthesis, six FIFO waiters, 30-second queue timeout and sixteen bounded connections. Authenticated prewarmed public clips alone bypass native synthesis/queue; private replies are never cached.

nodes.name: Local wake-word pilot
nodes.description: Optional host speech CLI: per-microphone KWS, bounded pre-roll and Silero VAD question capture, explicit Start/Stop and participant-only credentials. A 1200 ms post-wake continuation window retains a question after the wake's VAD endpoint; anchored ASR validation also accepts the spelling hay tina, never mid-sentence or empty questions. Opt-in run/run-file sends bounded WAV to the single-room speech coordinator; ordinary listen/file remain local. Wake is activation, not authentication. Default TTS remains Truc Ly. Room-wide polling suppresses KWS/pre-roll while busy; stale status/boot changes disarm until explicit restart; idle requires 800 ms quiet.

nodes.name: Optional single-room speech coordinator
nodes.description: Loopback pilot in clients/speech: authenticates enrolled participants through Gateway auth/me; server-held operator/STT keys; fixed approved meeting and documents; existing grounded Wiki ask and freshness checks; correlated Speak/Stop and terminal receipt polling. Volatile bounded turns, no stored audio/text; ambiguous playback stays disarmed. One central capture grant per room; atomic revision rejects delayed losing wakes; boot epoch fences old requests. Single process only.

Atomic leases and cache rechecks deduplicate viewers across API processes; completion reauthorizes and rechecks canonical source after inference. Private SQLite upgrade preserves cached results, active leases and legacy cooldowns; no transcript mutation.

Private worker completion metadata carries fixed failure codes only; partial or interrupted output is not accepted.

nodes.name: ASR host controller
nodes.description: Local host lifecycle bridge installed by make-all as an owned LaunchAgent on Mac or detached process on WSL2. Terminal verifies its auth cookie and forwards only the current user id with a derived control key. Identity owns per-account enabled/backend/revision preferences and aggregate demand; the controller starts and audio-tests known ASR workers before CAS preference commits. It serializes changes, waits ten idle seconds, conservatively retains both workers while any meeting bot or local Desktop capture exists, drains only with a distinct derived worker key and rechecks demand before stopping an owned Docker service or native MPS LaunchAgent. No arbitrary commands, endpoints, secret values or other user records reach the browser. A private state file records desired backend names and is rebuilt from Identity after restart. make-down stops the controller before shutting down services. Unavailable health or drain checks retain workers rather than force-stop.

nodes.name: Shared CPU meeting voice engine
nodes.description: Shared local speech primitives. Bot mode retains per-channel Silero VAD for endpoint/quiet events over bounded PCM IPC; a separate CPU LiveKit WakeWord 2.1.1 child verifies two retained local ONNX hashes (hey TINA and TINA ơi), shares sessions across independent channel streams and buffers 64 ms packets into 80 ms steps. KWS alone authorizes a caller; existing ASR supplies question text without rewriting transcript. Source/session/channel fences, bounded ASR history and same-caller continuation handle asynchronous delivery. Distinct known IDs on fresh independent channels can overlap without cancelling the selected caller; unknown/stale/duplicate identities still refuse ambiguous overlap. Fresh identified KWS can replace an idle post-answer follow-up slot with a new caller and conversation key, never preempt pending capture, thinking, playback or quiet. Successful playback opens an absolute 15-second same-channel known-participant follow-up window; unknown identity, Stop, source-policy change, expiry or playback failure never authorize it. Fast replies speak directly; only slow new requests receive a delayed 900 ms acknowledgment, never repeated on follow-ups. Local lexical pause cues extend incomplete utterances to a bounded two-second source-clock wait without an extra model. Busy VAD/ASR continues for explicit same-channel known-caller interruptions only; agreed/final fresh ASR rejects backchannels, other speakers and command phrases contained in played text. KWS stays locked. Stop cancels local playback and stale generation work; captured corrections survive quiet rearm. Monotonic sentence-completion receipts separate played prefixes from full generated proposals; stopped conversation history and cards use only confirmed completed sentences, never the in-progress sentence. Completed clarification history is context-only and source-fingerprint validated, enabling short clarification replies without inventing evidence. Missing participant metadata preserves continuous channel history; conflicting known IDs or source discontinuities reset it, without granting account identity or additional source permissions. Settings reads owner-only current-session KWS heartbeats; no heartbeat or old bot is not ready. Busy/quiet/Stop gate and clear KWS; missing assets, errors or backpressure refuse voice activation without interrupting transcript ASR. Weights are operator-provisioned in the existing read-only cache and never downloaded on join. Optional legacy host pilot retains its independent KWS path. Optional pinned WebRTC 0.3.1 CPU NS Low uses one state per capture channel, 10 ms FIFO processing and measured 96-sample delay compensation. AEC/HPF/AGC are verified off; original packet counts and source timestamps survive flush.

nodes.name: meeting-voice.v1 policy and turn protocol
nodes.description: Owner-approved room-shared sources and revision-checked policy; active meeting/session-bound bot capability. No participant account is inferred from voice or display names. Owner-approved ASR name variants are optional, revision-bound, and cannot use greeting prefixes; fixed base names are TINA/Tina/TINA ơi. Generic human-call alias anh ơi is rejected; suggested specific variants require owner approval. Optional bounded owner diagnostics carry original observation/heard timestamps and reason codes, independently expiring within 30s; legacy state messages remain valid. Revision-bound noise_suppression is boolean/default false, separate from room sharing; optional audio snapshot reports off/starting/low/failed. Owner-requested defaults are seeded on new capable transcribing Google Meet spawns: voice on, NS on, own transcript allowed, no documents. Existing saved policies survive continuation; absent policies are initialized. tin ơi is a fixed anchored case-insensitive invocation. ti na ơi, tiên na ơi, tinh anh ơi and tin anh ơi are also built-in anchored case-insensitive names by owner request, with no per-room Save. Custom alias records remain unchanged; raw ASR is never rewritten. After rearm, stale channel-onset windows admit only complete, ordered, text-aligned timed ASR speech intervals starting after the fence; wholly fresh source windows remain valid. Voice-only projection preserves raw ASR and request count. A confirmed name-only utterance receives the cached source-free acknowledgment without an LLM call, then after quiet rearm permits one same-channel fresh question before the five-second caller window expires. Known transport participant identity must match; missing identity remains channel-only. Acknowledgment, completed-answer and resumable-interruption caller continuation expire after 5s; later questions require a fresh wake. Stop/failure/policy change fences continuation and late ASR; follow-up answer omits a duplicate acknowledgment. During post-ack quiet gating, at most eight same-channel ASR hypotheses are retained and VAD continues endpoint tracking; quiet rearm replays only through existing source/participant fences. Pure acknowledgment echo is ignored. Voice answer completion uses a dedicated concise/clarifying prompt with BM25 relevance, recent 120-second transcript and adjacent evidence, bounded to 32 sources/24000 characters; long approved transcript/document sources are projected into deterministic <=1200-character chunks with 200-character overlap before ranking, with parent key/fingerprint, exact character offsets, speaker and unchanged parent time intervals. Owner/meeting/policy/key/fingerprint-scoped CPU-local multilingual-E5-small INT8 embeddings rank only the authorized chunks and fuse with BM25 via reciprocal ranks. A bounded 8192-vector/15-minute RAM cache and three-second cold indexing budget preserve voice latency; busy/failing semantic encoding retains BM25, with no private text sent to an embedding provider. Pinned ONNX/tokenizer assets and MIT notice are baked into Agent API. Whole-meeting recap intent separately covers every approved transcript chunk in chronological <=12-source/12000-character parts. Verified map facts are reduced in bounded groups, then final claims are checked against original plus related evidence. A 512-job/15-minute owner/meeting/policy/input-scoped RAM cache with three in-flight completions supports resumable summary_pending responses; incomplete preparation never claims whole-meeting coverage. All jobs recheck current source permissions before dispatch and final release fences changes to the complete input snapshot. Recaps are read-only derived output and do not edit canonical notes/transcript. Neighbor chunks supply context under the existing budgets; final source checks regenerate the same projection and parent changes revoke every affected chunk; no embeddings or external tools. Voice drafts receive an exact digit/date citation guard and a separate selected-model entailment/contradiction review. Identity, basic social/capability requests and unsupported external actions use fixed server-owned assistant responses with no meeting fact generation. Compound/ambiguous questions remain evidence-scoped and public web stays explicit. One rejected draft may be repaired using the same approved sources and must pass both checks again; supported partial answers may ask a short follow-up. Content-free verification codes (at most two) are stored with the owner-visible reply, never drafts or reviewer prose. Provider budgets share a 50-second scheduling deadline: generation up to 25s, each review/repair up to 10s; rejected/unavailable review never releases the unchecked draft. Optional owner-selected engine=tina|livekit defaults to tina. The three-meeting self-hosted Agents runtime uses confirmed ASR questions over custom HTTP I/O and sends PCM back through the existing bot playback; raw meeting audio and canonical transcripts stay on their original path. New bots advertise bridge support; legacy bots refuse the pilot instead of silently using native voice. VoiceTurnPermit is an internal boolean reply bound to the exact current request and active bot session, requiring both owner identity and the service secret. The 360-second exclusive reservation covers the bot total 330-second wait/playback budget. The bot announces a slow whole-meeting recap once using fixed cached local TTS, waits for the background result and automatically plays only its verified final answer. Transcript capture continues and existing Stop/caller/policy/generation fences refuse late results. nodes.name: Optional local LiveKit Agents pilot
nodes.description: Pinned LiveKit Agents 1.8.11 worker, up to three independent rooms and AgentSessions in one process. Custom LLM adapter uses capability-scoped TINA context/plan/lookup/final-answer endpoints; Agents executes up to two native SDK batches of two read-only tools selected by the configured LLM through TINA's credential boundary; custom TTS adapter calls shared VieNeu. No owner/provider API keys or workspace mounts. Whole-meeting recap requests skip keyword tool planning and use the source-authorized TINA map/reduce/verify recap flow; raw media ownership remains in the meeting bot. Supplemental tool planning sees prior results and may rewrite a private retrieval query or read surrounding original text using a per-turn opaque handle. The core limits two plans/four attempted tools to a shared 30-second retrieval phase; timeouts skip work and retain successful queries. Context handles are current-source fingerprint-bound, source permissions are rechecked, and Stop/final dispatch fence late results. SDK ChatContext is scoped by meeting/session/policy and hashed caller (32 callers, three turns, 15-minute expiry), refreshed from TINA's source-valid actual playback receipts before every turn. Generated but unheard text is discarded. TINA matches SDK context to heard history, controls source permissions, and verifies the final reply. PCM HTTP output is bounded and carries no microphone playback receipt. Stop UUID fences, disconnect cancellation, policy reaping and 90s idle cleanup apply. Raw room audio/text inputs, room transcript outputs and recording are disabled. LLM planning/tool/final failures release the core reservation and retire the SDK runtime for a fresh next turn. Per-request synthesis completion is tracked independently of SpeechHandle; partial TTS failure aborts the HTTP PCM stream without a success terminator. Header guards use pure ASGI to preserve transport errors. Cleanup claims the exact registry generation under the opening lock and each generation has a unique room name, preventing stale/delayed deletion of a replacement. Configuration distinguishes permission/session rejection from transient service errors: 401/403/404 deny, 409 invalidates, and other non-200 responses become 503. Transient errors preserve busy/recent rooms without authorizing new requests or bypassing source checks. The TINA background recap pool retains one exclusive voice turn while SDK LLM work waits up to 160 seconds and the HTTP answer route up to 165 seconds; progress announcements bypass the busy SDK session using shared fixed-message TTS. No new audio/RAG runtime or simultaneous room question is introduced. Capacity is three meetings in one replica/process; a fourth is refused. Authenticated /ready validates local TTS token and PCM metadata without inference; full capacity is not unhealthy. SDK PCM revalidates the current Redis turn via the capability-only Meeting API before synthesis, while streaming and at completion, including after SDK runtime recreation. Automated qualification opens three actual local rooms and fifteen uncached TTS streams over TCP with explicit synthetic meeting/LLM/receipt authority. Live meeting and actual model-provider acceptance remain separate. PCM admission belongs to the complete ASGI response lifetime; header-send and early disconnect failures close the iterator and release reserved lookahead credits, preventing a room from becoming permanently audio-busy.
